chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Abi Umayr from Haytham al-Sayrafi from a man from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)

Regarding a man who had a debt due from another man, and owed a debt himself, and the one who owed him died, and he was asked whether it is better to release him from the debt or not to release him, he said: 'Leave him, that is sufficient.'
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling when a creditor's debtor dies and the creditor also owes the deceased money?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) addresses the scenario of mutual debts where one party dies, advising the surviving creditor to 'leave it' (*da'hu*) rather than formally releasing the debt. This ruling highlights the Shia juristic preference for maintaining the status quo of mutual obligations to avoid unnecessary legal complexity or potential loss of rights, reflecting the principle of *istishab* (presumption of continuity) in debt settlements. It underscores the practical wisdom of allowing natural offsetting (*muqasasah*) to occur without requiring explicit formalities, a view supported by many Shia jurists in cases of ambiguous mutual indebtedness.
